newsitem.title: UK: Bosnia must comply with peace pact - EU official.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia must comply with peace pact - EU official.

text.p: A top European Union official said on Thursday he was not convinced Bosnian authorities would comply with peace terms and the international community must compel them to do so by "whatever means".

EU External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek, in hinting at the use of force, appeared to go beyond what was contained in a draft final document on a two-day peace conference ending in London later on Thursday.

That document told Bosnia's ethnic leaders they must fully implement the year-old Dayton peace pact and issue arrest warrants for war criminals or forfeit Western aid, but stopped short of calling for force to be used.

But van den Broek told a news conference: "If the responsibility is not going to be taken by the authorities there (in Bosnia) the international community should undertake those responsibilities by whatever means."
Peacekeeping duties in Bosnia are currently handled by NATO, which plans to scale down the number of troops there next year. The EU is not in a position to deploy forces of its own.

Van den Broek said he had not been convinced by the promises of Bosnian leaders at the conference that they were willing to comply with the Dayton accord on issues such the surrendering of war criminals for trial at the international court.
He said economic threats were clearly not shifting the Bosnian authorities in these areas, adding: "There must be more power behind this policy."
He said it was not for the EU Commission to say what extra pressure should be put upon the Bosnian authorities.

Van den Broek said an EU foreign ministers' meeting in Brussels on Friday was likely to put off the question of giving economic concessions to the government in Serbia because of disapproval at the policies of President Slobodan Milosevic.
The opposition has staged mass protests in Belgrade in protest at alleged ballot-rigging by Milosevic's ruling Socialists in last month's local elections.
Van den Broek also urged a resolution of the issue of war criminals still at large, saying there could be no real peace until the fugitives were brought to justice.
